newsitem.title: USA: Heart surgeon Debakey says Yeltsin okay.
newsitem.headline: Heart surgeon Debakey says Yeltsin okay.

text.p: U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Wednesday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin is doing well, despite rumours to the contrary.
DeBakey, who went to Moscow last month to examine Yeltsin, said he had regular communications with the team of Russian doctors attending the stricken president.
"I know he's okay. Everything is still fine," he told Reuters.
Financial markets were affected this week by rumours that Yeltsin had died.
"I don't understand these things...how in the world do these rumours get around?" DeBakey said.

Yeltsin is recuperating from earlier heart attacks and is scheduled to have bypass surgery in two months to improve blood flow to his heart. DeBakey, one of the world's foremost heart surgeons and the man who pioneered the bypass procedure, said after examining Yeltsin that he expected full recovery from the operation.

DeBakey said Russian cardiologist Renat Akchurin, who will perform the surgery on Yeltsin, was scheduled to come to Houston next week to familiarize himself with equipment that DeBakey is going to provide for the operation.

"He's really coming at my request in order to observe some of the backup support which we have and that I'm going to make available to them. I want him to be familiar with that," Debakey said. Akchurin once trained under the 88-year-old Debakey, who teaches at the Baylor College of Medicine in Houston.
Reports from Moscow said that Yeltsin had moved from a hospital to a sanatorium near the Russian capital so that he could be more physically active ahead of the surgery.
